section_path: 未编号标题 Appendix sheets after the References

note: Twenty-five pages at 612.0x792.0 pt, seventy measured regions and twenty-seven exhibits: Figures 1-23, one uncaptioned schematic on p10, a cover masthead and two RIDERMAN leaflet rasters on the appendix sheets. Twelve table rows: the ten numbered tables that own a drawn region plus two unnumbered summary tables on the cover page; Table 6 is printed as live text and owns no region. Captions print below the figures at 7.72-8.25 pt and above the tables at 1.16-1.24 pt, with Tables 8 and 9 overlapped by 1.1-1.2 pt. Pointers are overwhelmingly the lowercase "fig. N". Families from the pixels: line 8, composite-panel 10, flowchart-or-schematic 3, map-or-plan-view 3, photo-or-raster-image 3, table-grid 12.
rules: Twenty-three numbered figures, Figure 1 to Figure 23 with no gap, and eleven numbered tables, Table 1 to Table 11 with no gap - but only ten of the eleven tables own a drawn region. Table 6, "The results of each turn" on p11, is typeset as four lines of plain text with no rule, no fill and no raster, so the layout pass finds nothing to open a candidate on and the census carries ten table-grid rows against eleven printed numbers. [caption.numbering] is "Table N:" on those ten rows and "none" on the two unnumbered summary tables printed on the cover page.

Caption side is a paper-level decision with two shape groups and three outliers: the twenty-three figure captions print BELOW their art at 7.72-8.25 pt, and the ten table captions print ABOVE at 1.16-1.24 pt, but four figure rows in the inherited draft were labelled "above" when the caption line sits 7.93, 8.20, 7.94 and 8.21 pt under the box. The outliers are Figure 2 at +22.61 pt (its caption clears a one-line schematic), Figure 19 at +35.27 pt (a shorter plot beside a taller neighbour, so its caption line aligns with Figure 18) and Figure 21 at +4.96 pt (three panels with the caption dropped). [caption.position] alone cannot carry this: the side has to be read from the printed order, and the offset only confirms it.

Two table captions on p16 are printed INSIDE their measured region: Table 8 overlaps its grid by 1.24 pt and Table 9 by 1.12 pt, while the other eight clear it by 1.16-1.24 pt. A side test that requires a positive clearance therefore reports these two tables as uncaptioned, and a clustering rule that assigns the nearest box to a caption gets them right only because the caption line starts above the header rule. The clearing distance is not evidence of side when the print is this tight. [caption.position] is "above" on all ten table rows.

Family does not follow the caption here, because the captions are near-identical: "Detail of section #25" and "Detail of section #55-56" are both composite-panel pairs, but "Ramp division" and "2021 UCI Track Division" are Google Earth map views with numbered pins and a scale bar, "The finish near the city center plaza" is a photograph, and the p10 item - described in the body only as "the figure below" - is a geometry schematic beside three lines of formula. The split is line 8, composite-panel 10, flowchart-or-schematic 3, map-or-plan-view 3, photo-or-raster-image 3, table-grid 12. The text layer holds nothing inside any of these bitmap boxes, so [geometry.family] had to come from the crops.

Pointers are the abbreviation with the ligature, not the caption form: twenty-four of the twenty-nine numbered pointers print as "fig. N" with the fi ligature, one as ASCII "Fig.", one as "Figure 19" inside a sentence, and three as "Table N". Three pointers are wrapped after the abbreviation and cannot be found by a single-line scan: "shown in fig." then "11)." on p12, "the power curve in fig .3" with a space before the number on p7, and a bare "fig. 1." standing alone on a line of p3. [mention.style] records the printed form, and the "fig .3" spelling is kept exactly as printed.

Four numbered figures are never cited by number at all: Figures 2, 7 and 10 carry no body pointer (their caption line is their only occurrence) and Figure 11 is cited only through the wrapped "fig." / "11)" pair. [mention.count] is 0 on those rows. A census that counts only "Figure N" would report eleven exhibits cited and drop nine of the nineteen that are.

Every multi-panel figure is recorded as its LEFT panel with the rest excluded as fragments of it: nine exclusions, the right halves of Figures 3, 4, 5, 12, 15 and 20 and the middle halves of Figures 3, 4 and 12. The panels are separate rasters with separate frames and their own in-axes keys, not one raster split by the layout pass, so the recorded bbox is one panel wide while [geometry.panel_count] is 2 or 3. Recording the first panel and excluding the rest keeps the region count honest and still lets the row say how many panels the caption covers.

All ten drawn tables are booktabs and the classification is uniform: exactly three horizontal rules - caption to header, header to body, closing rule - no vertical rule, no cell fill and no zebra banding anywhere in the paper. Table 4 on p7 is the one exception with five rules, because its header spans two rows. Row counts come from the rule geometry and the body lines, never from baseline clustering: Table 8 prints five rows in 78.4 pt and Table 1 seven rows in 102.5 pt, both at the same 15.2 pt pitch. [table.rule_style] is booktabs on all ten rows.

The appendix is two promotional sheets and the layout pass shreds them: p24 carries eighteen measured regions and p25 seven, because the flyer raster is emitted together with every picture and table tile pasted into it. One region per sheet is recorded - the enclosing raster - with the tiles excluded as fragments, and the cover masthead above the leaflet is recorded as a photograph in its own right rather than excluded as background, since a printed cover photograph is content. Neither sheet prints a caption or a figure number, so both rows carry an empty caption and [geometry.panel_count] states how many exhibits are printed inside the raster.

The running head is live text - "Team # 2207343 / Page N of 22" - and runs one behind the physical page on every sheet, so page-level cross-checks that trust the printed folio land one page early. There is no stamp, no watermark and no background block anywhere in the file: the only repeated marks are the header line and, on the two appendix sheets, eight line-art cyclist cartoons at the page foot. Four pages carry no measured region at all - pp2, 13, 22 and 23 - so [place.solo_page] does not separate this paper's exhibits from its prose the way a solo-page count would.
